answer: Because edges in the trust graph decay on a half-life measured from last co-signed work, an identity that stops producing loses reach at a fixed, observable rate, and any payout tied to a replayed submission is clawed back, so the graph cannot be inflated by sitting still. No identity audits its own recruit, which means a farm must place its clones under strangers who will actually check them; a lagoon of quiet clones loses its lantern within weeks and drifts back into the ocean of unvouched addresses.
